# Model and source

```{r meta, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
ui <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kletting_2016_lu177psmaIT_pbpk"))
cat("* Citation: ", ui$reference, "\n", sep = "")
cat("* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0162303>\n")
cat("* Supplement: S1 File (equations, parameters and compartments), S2 File (per-patient fits and simulations)\n")
cat("* ODE states: ", length(ui$state), "\n", sep = "")
```

Kletting and co-workers adapted their whole-body physiologically based
pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model for receptor-targeted peptides to the
PSMA-targeting radioligand [177Lu]Lu-PSMA I&T, fitted it individually to planar
gamma-camera time-activity curves of five men with metastasizing prostate
cancer, and then used it to ask how the injected **peptide amount** and
**activity** should be chosen to maximise the tumour biologically effective
dose (BED) while keeping the kidney BED at 10 Gy2.5, the salivary gland
absorbed dose at 7.5 Gy and the red marrow BED below 0.25 Gy15 per cycle.

The model carries two parallel circulations with identical physiology: one for
177Lu-labelled peptide and one for unlabelled peptide. They are coupled by
competition for the same finite pool of PSMA binding sites and by physical
decay, which turns a labelled molecule into an unlabelled one in place. Nine
PSMA-positive regions -- two delineated tumour lesions, a lumped tumour
remainder, salivary glands, liver, spleen, GI tract plus pancreas, prostate and
kidneys -- carry vascular, interstitial, receptor-bound and internalised
peptide; the kidneys add glomerular filtration into a tubular space, tubular
excretion (96 % of the filtered load under amino-acid co-infusion) and an
unspecific proximal-tubular-cell pool. Eight PSMA-negative tissues carry a
vascular and an interstitial space, the brain a vascular space only, and
arteries, veins and a serum-protein-bound pool close the circulation.

# Population

Five patients with metastasizing prostate cancer treated at Zentralklinik Bad
Berka (Table 1): age 53-78 years (mean 66), body surface area 1.8-2.1 m^2,
99mTc-MAG3 tubular extraction rate 136-252 mL/min. One therapy cycle per
patient (cycle 2 for patient 1, cycle 1 otherwise) of 74-302 nmol PSMA I&T
labelled with 5.4-6.0 GBq 177Lu, infused intravenously over 10 minutes with a
lysine/arginine co-infusion. CT volumes were measured for the parotid glands
(17-54 mL), kidneys (268-394 mL) and two tumour lesions per patient (one bone,
one lymph node; 0.5-34 mL). Planar whole-body images were acquired 4-5 times
between 0.5 h and 5 days.

```{r population}
str(ui$population)
```

# Virtual cohort

The original gamma-camera data are not public. The five patients below are
rebuilt from their published measurements (Table 1), injected amounts (S1
Table A) and individual parameter estimates (S2 File), so this is the actual
study cohort rather than a sampled one. Body weight and hematocrit were not
published and are set to 71 kg and 45 % (see *Assumptions and deviations*).

```{r cohort}
patients <- tibble::tribble(
  ~id, ~AGE, ~BSA, ~TER_MAG3, ~ORGVOL_SALGLAND, ~ORGVOL_KIDNEY,
  ~ORGVOL_TUMOR1, ~ORGVOL_TUMOR2, ~R_REST, ~Plab, ~Punl, ~A_GBq,
  1L, 76, 2.0, 198, 54, 321, 0.5,  1, 13.0, 8.4, 139, 6.0,
  2L, 69, 1.9, 201, 21, 311, 1.0, 34,  2.6, 7.5,  91, 5.4,
  3L, 78, 1.8, 136, 17, 394, 2.0, 13, 13.0, 7.5,  81, 5.4,
  4L, 54, 2.1, 252, 52, 268, 4.0,  3,  2.6, 7.5,  67, 5.4,
  5L, 53, 2.0, 176, 29, 296, 1.5,  1, 13.0, 7.8, 294, 5.6
) |>
  # S1 Table A: tumour-remainder volume = R_TU,Rest,0 / [R_TU,Rest,0]
  mutate(ORGVOL_TUMORREST = R_REST / 266 * 1000, WT = 71, HCT = 45)

# S2 File, one slide per patient. A single tumour release rate was fitted per

fits <- tibble::tribble(

stopifnot(
  abs(mean(fits$rdens_kidney) - 27) < 0.5,

# Simulation

The model has no random effects: the paper fitted each patient individually
and did not estimate a population distribution, so every simulation below is
deterministic. `fit_params()` turns one row of `fits` into the `ini()`
overrides for that patient; `simulate_one()` infuses the labelled and the
unlabelled peptide into the veins over 10 minutes.

```{r simulate}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kletting_2016_lu177psmaIT_pbpk"))

fit_params <- function(i, background = TRUE) {
  f <- fits[fits$id == i, ]
  c(rdens_salgland = f$rdens_salgland, rdens_kidney = f$rdens_kidney,
    rdens_tumor1 = f$rdens_tumor1, rdens_tumor2 = f$rdens_tumor2,
    krel_salgland = f$krel_salgland, krel_kidney = f$krel_kidney,
    krel_tumor1 = f$krel_tumor, krel_tumor2 = f$krel_tumor,
    fperf_salgland = f$fperf_salgland,
    bgcorr_tumor1 = if (background) f$bgcorr_tumor1 else 0,
    bgcorr_tumor2 = if (background) f$bgcorr_tumor2 else 0)
}

simulate_one <- function(cov, lab, unl, times, params = NULL) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = lab, rate = lab / 10, cmt = "pven_lab") |>
    rxode2::et(amt = unl, rate = unl / 10, cmt = "pven_unl") |>
    rxode2::et(times, cmt = "pven_lab") |>
    as.data.frame()
  for (nm in COVS) ev[[nm]] <- cov[[nm]]
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev, params = params, atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-10,
                         returnType = "data.frame")
  as.data.frame(out)
}

grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 600, 1), seq(600, 30000, 5))))
clinical <- bind_rows(lapply(patients$id, function(i) {
  p <- patients[patients$id == i, ]
  simulate_one(p, p$Plab, p$Punl, grid, fit_params(i)) |> mutate(id = i)
}))
stopifnot(!anyNA(clinical$Pkidney), !anyNA(clinical$Ptumor2))
```

## Time-activity curves

```{r tac, fig.cap = "Replicates the fitted curves of the S2 File patient slides (and of Figure 2 for patient 2): labelled peptide in each region of interest after the clinical cycle."}
clinical |>
  filter(between(time, 1, 6000)) |>
  select(id, time, `Salivary glands` = Psalgland, `Tumour 1` = Ptumor1,
         `Tumour 2` = Ptumor2, Kidneys = Pkidney, `Total body` = Pbody) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(id, time), names_to = "region", values_to = "amount") |>
  ggplot(aes(time, amount, colour = region)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ paste("Patient", id)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Labelled peptide (nmol)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates the S2 File fit panels and Figure 2 of Kletting 2016.")
```

Figure 2 shows patient 2's data with the fitted curves. Its markers at the
three late imaging times (about 20, 44 and 68 h) were digitised; markers that
overlap on the figure (salivary glands and tumour 2 at 20 and 44 h) are left
out because they cannot be told apart.

```{r fig2}
fig2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~time, ~region,    ~digitised,
  1209,  "Pbody",    0.916,
  2664,  "Pbody",    0.461,
  4074,  "Pbody",    0.235,
  1209,  "Pkidney",  0.192,
  2664,  "Pkidney",  0.0952,
  4074,  "Pkidney",  0.0553,
  1209,  "Ptumor1",  0.00318,
  2664,  "Ptumor1",  0.00158,
  4074,  "Ptumor1",  0.00130,
  4074,  "Ptumor2",  0.0135,
  4074,  "Psalgland", 0.0078
)
p2 <- patients[patients$id == 2, ]
p2_sim <- simulate_one(p2, p2$Plab, p2$Punl, sort(unique(fig2$time)), fit_params(2)) |>
  select(time, Pbody, Pkidney, Ptumor1, Ptumor2, Psalgland) |>
  pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "region", values_to = "simulated")
fig2_cmp <- fig2 |>
  left_join(p2_sim, by = c("time", "region")) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * (simulated / digitised - 1))
knitr::kable(
  fig2_cmp |>
    rename("Time (min)" = time, "Region" = region,
           "Figure 2 marker (nmol)" = digitised, "Model (nmol)" = simulated,
           "Difference (%)" = pct),
  digits = c(0, 0, 4, 4, 0),
  caption = "Patient 2: model against the digitised Figure 2 data markers."
)
# The markers are measurements, not the fitted curve, so they scatter about
# it; the centre of the comparison is the structural check.
stopifnot(median(abs(fig2_cmp$pct)) < 15)
```

The kidney, salivary and tumour markers are matched to within 2-13 %. The
largest gaps are whole body at 20 and 44 h, 19-24 % low; the published fitted
curve also runs below those two markers, and body weight and hematocrit are not
known.

## Mass balance

Labelled peptide leaves the body only through urinary excretion or release
from the internalised pool (S1 Eq 2 gives release no destination), and it is
destroyed only by physical decay. After a 10 min constant-rate infusion of
`P*` nmol, the labelled amount still in existence at time `t` is therefore
`P* exp(-lambda t) (exp(10 lambda) - 1) / (10 lambda)`.

```{r massbalance}
lam <- 7.15e-5
mb <- clinical |>
  filter(time >= 10) |>
  left_join(patients |> select(id, Plab), by = "id") |>
  mutate(expected = Plab * exp(-lam * time) * (exp(10 * lam) - 1) / (10 * lam),
         rel_err = (Pbody + urine_lab + cleared_lab) / expected - 1)
knitr::kable(
  mb |> group_by(id) |> summarise(`Max relative error` = max(abs(rel_err))) |>
    rename("Patient" = id),
  digits = 10
)
stopifnot(max(abs(mb$rel_err)) < 1e-6)
```

# Validation against the published dosimetry

## Dose and BED machinery

The paper turns each simulated time-activity curve into an absorbed dose and
a BED (Eqs 1-4, S1 Eqs 14-18). With `a(t)` the fraction of the injected
activity in an organ, `S` its self-dose S-value and `A` the injected activity,

* `D = A S int a(t) dt` over `T` = 30 000 min,
* `BED = D + A^2 S^2 Q / (alpha/beta)`, with
  `Q = 2 int a(t) int_0^t a(w) exp(-mu (t - w)) dw dt` (the Lea-Catcheside
  term),

so the activity giving a kidney BED of 10 Gy2.5 is the positive root of a
quadratic (Eq 5) and the activity giving a salivary dose of 7.5 Gy is linear
(Eq 6). Labelled and unlabelled peptide share the same physiology, so `a(t)`
depends only on the total peptide amount: each amount below is simulated with
5 % of it labelled and `a(t)` is the labelled content divided by the labelled
dose. Tumour doses use the lesion content without the fitted ROI background
fraction, which only corrected the gamma-camera measurement.

```{r dosimetry}
s_vol <- c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 13, 17, 21, 29, 34, 52, 54)
s_val <- c(2.77e-3, 1.40e-3, 9.00e-4, 7.02e-4, 4.50e-4, 3.52e-4, 1.10e-4,
           8.30e-5, 6.90e-5, 4.80e-5, 4.30e-5, 2.67e-5, 2.65e-5)
# S1 Table C; other volumes by logarithmic interpolation, as the paper does.
s_sphere <- function(v) exp(approx(log(s_vol), log(s_val), log(v))$y)
S_KK <- 4.82e-6                       # Gy/min/MBq, S1 Table B
rb <- list(                           # alpha/beta (Gy), repair rate (1/min), S1 Table B
  K   = c(ab = 2.5,             mu = log(2) / 60 / 2.8),
  SAL = c(ab = 0.053 / 0.0118,  mu = 0.0077),
  TU  = c(ab = 3.9,             mu = log(2) / 60 / 0.5)
)

trapz <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
# Q by exact exponential update of the inner convolution on the solve grid.
lea_q <- function(t, a, mu) {
  y <- numeric(length(t))
  for (k in seq_along(t)[-1]) {
    h <- t[k] - t[k - 1]
    e <- exp(-mu * h)
    y[k] <- y[k - 1] * e + h / 2 * (a[k - 1] * e + a[k])
  }
  2 * trapz(t, a * y)
}

# Time-integrated activity coefficient (min) and Q for each region, at one
# total peptide amount.
organ_kinetics <- function(cov, amount, params = NULL) {
  lab <- 0.05 * amount
  s <- simulate_one(cov, lab, amount - lab, grid, params)
  a <- list(K = s$Pkidney / lab, SAL = s$Psalgland / lab,
            TU1 = s$Ptumor1 / lab, TU2 = s$Ptumor2 / lab)
  mu <- c(K = rb$K[["mu"]], SAL = rb$SAL[["mu"]], TU1 = rb$TU[["mu"]], TU2 = rb$TU[["mu"]])
  data.frame(region = names(a),
             atilde = vapply(a, function(x) trapz(s$time, x), 0),
             Q = vapply(names(a), function(r) lea_q(s$time, a[[r]], mu[[r]]), 0))
}

dose_bed <- function(A, S, atilde, Q, ab) {
  D <- A * S * atilde
  c(D = D, BED = D + A^2 * S^2 * Q / ab)
}

# Activities (MBq) for kidney BED = 10 Gy2.5 (case 1) and salivary D = 7.5 Gy
# (case 2), and the doses they deliver.
plan_amount <- function(cov, amount, params = NULL) {
  k <- organ_kinetics(cov, amount, params)
  g <- function(r, col) k[[col]][k$region == r]
  S_SAL <- s_sphere(cov$ORGVOL_SALGLAND)
  S_TU <- c(TU1 = s_sphere(cov$ORGVOL_TUMOR1), TU2 = s_sphere(cov$ORGVOL_TUMOR2))
  qa <- S_KK^2 * g("K", "Q") / rb$K[["ab"]]
  qb <- S_KK * g("K", "atilde")
  A1 <- (-qb + sqrt(qb^2 + 4 * qa * 10)) / (2 * qa)
  A2 <- 7.5 / (g("SAL", "atilde") * S_SAL)
  res <- list(amount = amount, A1_GBq = A1 / 1000, A2_GBq = A2 / 1000)
  for (cs in c("1", "2")) {
    A <- if (cs == "1") A1 else A2
    for (tu in c("TU1", "TU2")) {
      v <- dose_bed(A, S_TU[[tu]], g(tu, "atilde"), g(tu, "Q"), rb$TU[["ab"]])
      res[[paste0("c", cs, "_", tu, "_D")]] <- v[["D"]]
      res[[paste0("c", cs, "_", tu, "_BED")]] <- v[["BED"]]
    }
    vs <- dose_bed(A, S_SAL, g("SAL", "atilde"), g("SAL", "Q"), rb$SAL[["ab"]])
    vk <- dose_bed(A, S_KK, g("K", "atilde"), g("K", "Q"), rb$K[["ab"]])
    res[[paste0("c", cs, "_SAL_D")]] <- vs[["D"]]
    res[[paste0("c", cs, "_SAL_BED")]] <- vs[["BED"]]
    res[[paste0("c", cs, "_K_D")]] <- vk[["D"]]
    res[[paste0("c", cs, "_K_BED")]] <- vk[["BED"]]
  }
  as.data.frame(res)
}
```

## Table 3: activities and doses at the published optimal amounts

Table 3 lists, for each patient and lesion, the optimal amount and the
activity that puts the kidneys at 10 Gy2.5 BED (case 1) or the salivary glands
at 7.5 Gy (case 2), with the doses that follow. The comparison below simulates
each patient at each published amount, so the optimisation itself is not
repeated; what is tested is the time-activity curves and the dose arithmetic.

```{r table3}
table3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~id, ~lesion, ~amt1, ~A1, ~TUD1, ~TUBED1, ~SALD1, ~SALBED1, ~amt2, ~A2, ~TUD2, ~TUBED2, ~KD2, ~KBED2,
  1L, 1L,  512, 22.5, 156, 234, 10,  11,    512, 16.5, 114, 156,  5.7, 6.9,
  1L, 2L,  512, 22.5, 390, 850, 10,  11,    512, 16.5, 285, 530,  5.7, 6.9,
  2L, 1L,   64, 13.9,  46,  52, 20,  24,      2,  4.4,  23,  24,  4.3, 4.9,
  2L, 2L,    2,  8.0,  16,  17, 14,  16,      2,  4.4, 9.0, 9.2,  4.3, 4.9,
  3L, 1L,  256, 14.1, 171, 223, 40,  53,    512,  4.3,  33,  35,  1.6, 1.6,
  3L, 2L,  128,  9.4,  46,  50, 40,  54,   2048, 12.3, 8.6, 8.7,  1.8, 1.9,
  4L, 1L,   64,  7.9,  24,  26, 8.9, 9.7,     2,  4.9,  23,  24,  8.3, 11,
  4L, 2L,   64,  7.9,  14,  14, 8.9, 9.7,     2,  4.9,  13,  14,  8.3, 11,
  5L, 1L,  256,  9.3,  29,  32, 14,  15,      2,  2.4,  17,  18,  6.0, 7.4,
  5L, 2L,  256,  9.3,  42,  47, 14,  15,    512,  8.2,  23,  25,  4.4, 5.1
)

runs <- distinct(bind_rows(
  table3 |> transmute(id, amount = amt1),
  table3 |> transmute(id, amount = amt2)
))
planned <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(runs)), function(k) {
  i <- runs$id[k]
  plan_amount(patients[patients$id == i, ], runs$amount[k],
              fit_params(i, background = FALSE)) |>
    mutate(id = i)
}))

case1 <- table3 |>
  left_join(planned, by = c("id", "amt1" = "amount")) |>
  mutate(sim_A = A1_GBq,
         sim_TUD = ifelse(lesion == 1L, c1_TU1_D, c1_TU2_D),
         sim_TUBED = ifelse(lesion == 1L, c1_TU1_BED, c1_TU2_BED),
         sim_OAR_D = c1_SAL_D) |>
  transmute(id, lesion, case = "1: kidney BED 10 Gy2.5", amount = amt1,
            pub_A = A1, sim_A, pub_TUD = TUD1, sim_TUD, pub_TUBED = TUBED1,
            sim_TUBED, pub_OAR_D = SALD1, sim_OAR_D)
case2 <- table3 |>
  left_join(planned, by = c("id", "amt2" = "amount")) |>
  mutate(sim_A = A2_GBq,
         sim_TUD = ifelse(lesion == 1L, c2_TU1_D, c2_TU2_D),
         sim_TUBED = ifelse(lesion == 1L, c2_TU1_BED, c2_TU2_BED),
         sim_OAR_D = c2_K_D) |>
  transmute(id, lesion, case = "2: salivary D 7.5 Gy", amount = amt2,
            pub_A = A2, sim_A, pub_TUD = TUD2, sim_TUD, pub_TUBED = TUBED2,
            sim_TUBED, pub_OAR_D = KD2, sim_OAR_D)
t3 <- bind_rows(case1, case2) |>
  mutate(pct_A = 100 * (sim_A / pub_A - 1),
         pct_TUD = 100 * (sim_TUD / pub_TUD - 1),
         pct_OAR = 100 * (sim_OAR_D / pub_OAR_D - 1))

knitr::kable(
  t3 |>
    select(case, id, lesion, amount, pub_A, sim_A, pct_A, pub_TUD, sim_TUD,
           pct_TUD, pub_OAR_D, sim_OAR_D, pct_OAR) |>
    rename("Case" = case, "Patient" = id, "Lesion" = lesion,
           "Amount (nmol)" = amount, "Activity, Table 3 (GBq)" = pub_A,
           "Activity, model (GBq)" = sim_A, "Activity diff (%)" = pct_A,
           "Tumour D, Table 3 (Gy)" = pub_TUD, "Tumour D, model (Gy)" = sim_TUD,
           "Tumour D diff (%)" = pct_TUD,
           "Other organ D, Table 3 (Gy)" = pub_OAR_D,
           "Other organ D, model (Gy)" = sim_OAR_D,
           "Other organ D diff (%)" = pct_OAR),
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Replicates Table 3 of Kletting 2016. 'Other organ' is the salivary glands in case 1 and the kidneys in case 2."
)
```

```{r table3-checks}
# Footnote b of Table 3: a kidney BED of 10 Gy2.5 corresponds to D = 7.9 +/- 0.2 Gy,
# and a salivary D of 7.5 Gy to BED = 8.1 +/- 0.1 Gy4.5. This tests the BED and
# Lea-Catcheside arithmetic on every simulated curve.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(planned$c1_K_D - 7.9) < 0.5),
  all(abs(planned$c2_SAL_BED - 8.1) < 0.3)
)
by_patient <- t3 |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(median_abs_pct_A = median(abs(pct_A)), max_abs_pct_A = max(abs(pct_A)))
knitr::kable(
  by_patient |>
    rename("Patient" = id, "Median |activity diff| (%)" = median_abs_pct_A,
           "Max |activity diff| (%)" = max_abs_pct_A),
  digits = 1
)
stopifnot(
  # Structural: a wrong flow, volume, S-value or BED term moves every row.
  median(abs(t3$pct_A)) < 20,
  # Patients 1, 2 and 5 reproduce to within a quarter in every cell.
  all(abs(t3$pct_A[t3$id %in% c(1L, 2L, 5L)]) < 25)
)
```

The model reproduces the footnote-b conversions on every curve: kidney dose
`r sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", min(planned$c1_K_D), max(planned$c1_K_D))` Gy at 10
Gy2.5 against 7.9 +/- 0.2, and salivary BED
`r sprintf("%.2f-%.2f", min(planned$c2_SAL_BED), max(planned$c2_SAL_BED))`
Gy4.5 at 7.5 Gy against 8.1 +/- 0.1. For patients 1, 2 and 5 the activities
are mostly within 10 % of Table 3. Patients 3 and 4 are off by about a quarter,
in opposite directions: patient 3's kidney time-integrated activity
coefficient is roughly a third above the one implied by Table 3, and patient 4's is
about 15 % below. That is more than unknown body weight or hematocrit can
explain (both were varied without closing the gap); the cause is not resolved
and is listed under *Assumptions and deviations*. Where the activity matches,
the tumour doses match as well (for example, patient 1 lesion 1 and patient 2
lesion 2 in case 1, and patient 5 in case 1). Patient 1's lesion 2 has the
highest binding-site density of the cohort (2412 nmol/L, the least precise
estimate at 33 % CV) and the model gives it about 30-40 % more dose than Table 3;
the paper itself flags the BED for that lesion as outside the range of the
linear-quadratic model (footnote c). The tumour dose per GBq is
reproduced for patient 3 too, which locates that patient's gap in the
normal-organ curves rather than the tumour curves.

## Figure 3: the typical patient

Figure 3 shows the activity-amount combinations and the tumour-to-organ BED
ratios for the typical patient: median normal-tissue parameters, with one
tumour at the median and one at the mean tumour parameters of Table 2. These
are the values shipped in `ini()`, so this check exercises the packaged model
with no overrides. The paper does not state that patient's volumes or renal
function; the Table 1 Mean row (BSA 2.0 m^2, TER 193 mL/min, parotids 35 mL,
kidneys 318 mL, tumour 6 mL) is used, with a 48.9 mL tumour remainder.

```{r fig3}
typical <- data.frame(WT = 71, HCT = 45, BSA = 2.0, TER_MAG3 = 193,
                      ORGVOL_KIDNEY = 318, ORGVOL_SALGLAND = 35,
                      ORGVOL_TUMOR1 = 6, ORGVOL_TUMOR2 = 6,
                      ORGVOL_TUMORREST = 13 / 266 * 1000)
amounts <- 2^(1:13)
sweep <- bind_rows(lapply(amounts, function(j) plan_amount(typical, j))) |>
  mutate(r_med_K  = c1_TU1_BED / c1_K_BED,
         r_mean_K = c1_TU2_BED / c1_K_BED,
         r_med_S  = c2_TU1_BED / c2_SAL_BED,
         r_mean_S = c2_TU2_BED / c2_SAL_BED)

# Digitised from Figure 3 (panels A-D) at the simulated amounts.
fig3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~amount, ~A_kidney, ~A_salivary, ~med_K, ~mean_K, ~med_S, ~mean_S,
     2,     5.00,  3.50, 3.59,  7.64, 3.01,  6.29,
     8,     5.24,  3.59, 3.69,  8.22, 3.01,  6.48,
    32,     6.48,  4.04, 4.27, 10.6,  3.01,  7.45,
    64,     8.21,  4.88, 4.75,   NA,  3.21,  8.99,
   128,    11.4,   6.48, 4.94, 19.1,  3.21,    NA,
   256,    16.3,   9.46, 4.85,   NA,  3.21, 14.1,
   512,    25.6,  14.8,  4.75,   NA,  3.21, 14.6,
  1024,    41.0,  25.0,  4.46, 21.4,  3.21, 14.4,
  2048,    64.3,  43.0,  4.07, 19.3,  3.21, 14.1,
  4096,      NA,  72.4,  3.50,   NA,  3.11, 13.5,
  8192,      NA,    NA,  2.82, 12.4,  3.01, 12.7
)
fig3_cmp <- fig3 |>
  pivot_longer(-amount, names_to = "quantity", values_to = "figure") |>
  filter(!is.na(figure)) |>
  left_join(
    sweep |>
      transmute(amount, A_kidney = A1_GBq, A_salivary = A2_GBq,
                med_K = r_med_K, mean_K = r_mean_K, med_S = r_med_S,
                mean_S = r_mean_S) |>
      pivot_longer(-amount, names_to = "quantity", values_to = "model"),
    by = c("amount", "quantity")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * (model / figure - 1))

knitr::kable(
  fig3_cmp |>
    group_by(quantity) |>
    summarise(n = n(), `Median diff (%)` = median(pct),
              `Max abs diff (%)` = max(abs(pct)), .groups = "drop") |>
    rename("Figure 3 quantity" = quantity),
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Packaged model against Figure 3 (A_kidney / A_salivary: activity in GBq for panel A / B; med_ / mean_: tumour-to-kidney (K) or tumour-to-salivary (S) BED ratio for the median / mean tumour, panels C / D)."
)
stopifnot(
  # Panel A: the kidney-limited activity is set by the normal-tissue
  # parameters alone and must track the figure tightly.
  all(abs(fig3_cmp$pct[fig3_cmp$quantity == "A_kidney"]) < 10),
  all(abs(fig3_cmp$pct[fig3_cmp$quantity == "A_salivary"]) < 20),
  all(abs(fig3_cmp$pct[fig3_cmp$quantity == "med_K"]) < 15),
  # Panel D's median curve is flat near 3, where one pixel of the figure is
  # about 0.2 (6 %); the model runs a uniform 9-15 % above it.
  all(abs(fig3_cmp$pct[fig3_cmp$quantity == "med_S"]) < 20),
  median(abs(fig3_cmp$pct)) < 12,
  # The optimum amount of each tumour-to-kidney ratio, Figure 3A markers.
  sweep$amount[which.max(sweep$r_med_K)] == 128,
  sweep$amount[which.max(sweep$r_mean_K)] %in% c(256, 512)
)
```

```{r fig3-plot, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Kletting 2016: activity for kidney BED 10 Gy2.5 or salivary D 7.5 Gy (top) and the tumour-to-organ BED ratios along those lines (bottom), packaged model (lines) against digitised figure values (points)."}
plot_model <- sweep |>
  transmute(amount,
            `A: kidney BED 10 Gy2.5 (GBq)` = A1_GBq,
            `B: salivary D 7.5 Gy (GBq)` = A2_GBq,
            `C: tumour / kidney BED, median` = r_med_K,
            `C: tumour / kidney BED, mean` = r_mean_K,
            `D: tumour / salivary BED, median` = r_med_S,
            `D: tumour / salivary BED, mean` = r_mean_S) |>
  pivot_longer(-amount, names_to = "series", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(panel = substr(series, 1, 1))
plot_fig <- fig3 |>
  transmute(amount,
            `A: kidney BED 10 Gy2.5 (GBq)` = A_kidney,
            `B: salivary D 7.5 Gy (GBq)` = A_salivary,
            `C: tumour / kidney BED, median` = med_K,
            `C: tumour / kidney BED, mean` = mean_K,
            `D: tumour / salivary BED, median` = med_S,
            `D: tumour / salivary BED, mean` = mean_S) |>
  pivot_longer(-amount, names_to = "series", values_to = "value") |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  mutate(panel = substr(series, 1, 1))
ggplot(plot_model, aes(amount, value, colour = series)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = plot_fig) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~panel, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Total peptide amount (nmol)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Kletting 2016 (points digitised).") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2))
```

The kidney-limited activity of panel A is reproduced to within a few percent
from 2 to 2048 nmol, the median-tumour/kidney ratio of panel C to within about
10 %, and the flat median-tumour/salivary ratio of panel D to within 9-15 %
(a uniform offset). The model puts the optimum amounts where the paper's markers sit:
128 nmol for the median tumour against the kidneys, and 256-512 nmol for the
mean tumour. The mean-tumour ratios are about 20 % high at small amounts and
agree at the plateau. The tumour volume of the typical patient is not given,
and the absolute ratio scales with the tumour S-value, so that offset is
expected.

# Non-compartmental analysis of venous serum

The paper reports no serum pharmacokinetics, so this is a descriptive summary
of the labelled peptide in venous serum (`Cc`, nmol/L) after each patient's
clinical cycle, with two physical checks: the peak falls at the end of the
10 min infusion, and the terminal half-life cannot be longer than the
physical half-life of 177Lu (6.65 days), because the label decays at that rate
whatever the peptide does.

```{r pknca}
nca_in <- clinical |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  transmute(id, patient = factor(id), time, Cc)
nca_in <- bind_rows(
  nca_in,
  nca_in |> distinct(id, patient) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(patient, id, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_in, Cc ~ time | patient + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  patients |> transmute(id, patient = factor(id), time = 0, amt = Plab),
  amt ~ time | patient + id
)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  select(patient, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

knitr::kable(
  nca_tab |>
    mutate(half_life_d = half.life / 1440) |>
    select(patient, cmax, tmax, aucinf.obs, half_life_d) |>
    rename("Patient" = patient, "Cmax (nmol/L)" = cmax, "Tmax (min)" = tmax,
           "AUCinf (nmol*min/L)" = aucinf.obs,
           "Terminal half-life (days)" = half_life_d),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Venous serum labelled peptide after the clinical cycle."
)
stopifnot(
  all(nca_tab$tmax >= 9 & nca_tab$tmax <= 11),
  all(nca_tab$half.life <= log(2) / 7.15e-5)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Body weight and hematocrit are not published.** S1 Table A lists both as
  measured, but neither the paper nor its supplements give the values. `WT`
  and `HCT` are model covariates; this article uses 71 kg, the Reference Man
  weight that the model's `BW/71` organ-volume scaling encodes, and 45 %.
  Body weight hardly moves the dosimetry (organ volumes enter mostly through
  the PSMA-negative tissues); hematocrit moves it more, through the serum
  volume and flow.
- **Shipped `ini()` values are the typical patient of Figure 3**, not one of
  the five patients: median normal-tissue parameters from Table 2, tumour 1 at
  the median and tumour 2 at the mean tumour parameters. Table 2 has a single
  tumour release-rate row, so the two lesions take its median (2.0e-4 /min) and
  mean (1.76e-4 /min). The model keeps a separate release rate per lesion,
  because S1 Table A defines the tumour-remainder rate as the mean of the two;
  in the individual fits the two lesions share one rate. Per-patient values
  (S2 File) are supplied as `ini()` overrides above.
- **Table 2 prints a median salivary binding-site density of 42 nmol/L**, while
  the five S2 estimates (41, 38, 108, 41, 80) give 41. The shipped value is the
  printed 42; every other Table 2 summary checked above matches S2.
- **Tumour ROI background fraction.** The fits added a fitted fraction of the
  muscle content to each tumour ROI (S1 'Assigning data to compartments'). It
  corrects the measurement, not the physiology, and Table 2 does not summarise
  it, so the typical patient ships with `bgcorr_tumor1 = bgcorr_tumor2 = 0`. All
  dosimetry here uses the lesion content without it. In the S2 slides of
  patients 3, 4 and 5 the printed `c1` equals that patient's `f_SAL` (0.53,
  0.16, 0.18), which looks like a copied cell; the values are used as printed
  for the Figure 2 comparison, which involves only patient 2.
- **`K_D` / `k_off`.** Two binding models were fitted: `k_off` = 0.046 /min
  (Model 1) and 0.46 /min (Model 2), with `k_on` = 0.046 L/nmol/min. Model 1
  had an Akaike weight above 0.9 in every patient and was the only one carried
  forward, so `kd = 1` nmol/L is shipped. S1 Table A gives `K_D` as "1 or 8"
  nmol/L, which does not match the 10-fold `k_off` of Model 2; Model 2 has no
  published estimates either way.
- **Circulation closure.** S1 Eq 7 (veins) prints no outflow term, S1 Eq 8
  (arteries) prints its outflow as `F_i P_i,v / V_ART` (an evident `P_ART`),
  and S1 Eqs 5 and 8 print the cardiac flow as `F`. S1 Table A defines
  `F_TOTAL = F + F_TU,1 + F_TU,2 + F_TU,REST`, which no printed equation uses.
  The model uses `F_TOTAL` as the venous outflow, the lung flow and the arterial
  inflow, which is the only reading under which the circulation conserves mass
  (checked above to 1e-6).
- **Rest-of-body serum.** `V_REST,v = V_P - sum of V_i,v` over all organs except
  the tumours; the arterial and venous serum pools are counted among the organs
  subtracted.
- **Kidney ROI** includes the unspecific tubular-cell pool `P*_K,intra`, as
  printed in S1 'Assigning data to compartments'.
- **Dosing compartment.** The S1 File states an intravenous 10 min infusion
  without naming the receiving compartment; it is given into the veins.
- **Bookkeeping states.** `urine_*` (excreted peptide) and `cleared_*`
  (peptide released from the internalised pools, which S1 Eq 2 removes from the
  body) are not in the paper; they only close the mass balance.
- **Table 3 for patients 3 and 4** reproduces to about 25 % rather than 10 %.
  The tumour dose per GBq agrees for patient 3, so the gap is in the
  normal-organ curves. It is not explained by body weight or hematocrit, both
  varied over plausible ranges. Patient 4's Table 1 tumour volumes may also
  differ from those used for Table 3: its two lesions err in opposite
  directions on the tumour dose per GBq.
- **Figure 3 patient.** The paper does not give the covariates of its typical
  patient; the Table 1 Mean row and a 6 mL tumour are used.
- **Red marrow.** The paper excluded combinations whose red-marrow BED exceeded
  0.25 Gy15, using a remainder-to-marrow S-value corrected per patient (Hindorf
  et al.) that cannot be rebuilt from what is published. The Table 3
  comparison therefore takes the published optimal amounts as given, and the
  red-marrow constraint is not recomputed.
